identity.reason: A drawer is not a member of dialog, and one fact decides it: a persistent drawer has no dialog role at all. An alert dialog is a dialog — same role family, same keyboard, same modality — so a consumer writing [data-ui='dialog'] means it too. An inline drawer is a region of the page, nothing is inert, nothing is contained, and role=dialog on it would be the claim the APG calls severe
identity.cost: The header's three columns, the words' overflow handling, the close button's geometry and the forced-colours rule are shapes dialog already holds, and packages/styles/src/identity.test.mjs forbids reaching for them. Around eighty lines are written twice, and the two families can move apart without one breaking the other

wiring.role: dialog on the panel part under mode=overlay. Under mode=inline the panel writes no role: a navigation drawer is a navigation landmark and a filter panel is complementary, and a family that cannot know which one guesses wrong half the time. The consumer names it with render or with their own element
wiring.aria-modal: true on the panel only while modal is true, which is the only state in which the family makes the background inert. modal is fixed at false under mode=inline
wiring.aria-labelledby: the panel names its title part; a consumer who writes their own aria-label instead keeps it
wiring.aria-describedby: the panel names its description part when a description part is present
wiring.aria-haspopup: dialog on the trigger under mode=overlay only. An inline drawer is a disclosure, not a popup, and the property would promise a layer that never arrives
wiring.aria-expanded: true on the trigger while the drawer is open, in both modes
wiring.aria-controls: the trigger names the panel part
wiring.aria-busy: true on the body while the family is loading
wiring.resizerRole: separator on the resizer part, with tabindex=0, which is the focusable widget form the separator role takes
wiring.resizerValue: aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax on the resizer are the extent fraction times a hundred, rounded. The Window Splitter pattern calls 0 to 100 the typical range
wiring.resizerName: aria-labelledby the title part, which is the pattern's rule that the separator is named for the pane it sizes; a consumer with no title writes aria-label on the resizer
wiring.resizerControls: aria-controls on the resizer names the panel, which is the pattern's primary pane
wiring.aria-orientation: vertical on the resizer for side=start and side=end, horizontal for side=top and side=bottom

keyboard.effect: moves to the next tabbable element inside the panel, and wraps from the last to the first while modal
keyboard.focus: the next tabbable element inside the panel

keyboard.effect: moves to the previous tabbable element inside the panel, and wraps from the first to the last while modal
keyboard.focus: the previous tabbable element inside the panel

keyboard.effect: asks the topmost layer to close, carrying the reason escape; a layer that refuses stops the request reaching the layer beneath it, so one Escape never closes two
keyboard.focus: returns to the element that held it when the drawer opened

keyboard.effect: on the resizer, moves the separator one step to the left of the screen, which grows an end panel in a left-to-right document and shrinks it in a mirrored one; with snap points it moves to the adjacent stop
on the resizer, moves the separator one step to the right of the screen; with snap points it moves to the adjacent stop
on the resizer, moves the separator one step up the screen, which grows a bottom panel and shrinks a top one; with snap points it moves to the adjacent stop
on the resizer, moves the separator one step down the screen; with snap points it moves to the adjacent stop
on the resizer, gives the panel its smallest allowed extent
on the resizer, gives the panel its largest allowed extent

on the resizer, collapses the panel to its smallest allowed extent, and from there restores the extent it left. It does not close the drawer, because Escape already means that and a reader pressing Enter on a separator expects the separator to still be there

focus.contain: under mode=overlay while modal, from @slotted/core/focus. An inline drawer contains nothing and a non-modal overlay contains nothing, because both are reachable from the page by definition
focus.initial: the first tabbable element under mode=overlay; nothing at all under mode=inline, because a sidebar that stole focus every time a breakpoint crossed would be unusable. Angular Material takes the same split, defaulting autoFocus to false in side mode
focus.restore: the element that held focus when the drawer opened, or its nearest connected ancestor when that element has since left the document. It restores in both modes, and only when focus is still inside the panel or on the body, so closing a drawer the reader had already left moves nothing
focus.closedPanel: inert and content-visibility: hidden, in both modes. A panel the eye reads as closed whose controls are still in the tab sequence is the defect MUI's persistent variant ships

result.reason: What the platform calls returnValue and Angular Material returns from afterClosed(). It rides on the close request rather than declaring a second state model: nothing about a result is controlled, there is no initial one, and a consumer owning it would own a value only the family can produce

declinedReasons.submit: alertDialog owns a part whose meaning is confirmation and this family owns none. A drawer's Apply button is the consumer's own control, and it closes the drawer by setting open or by calling the handle

anatomy.root: the layer under mode=overlay — fixed to the viewport, stacked with --slotted-z-index-overlay plus the depth dismissable-layer writes — and the flow box under mode=inline, whose own size is what transitions. A one-cell grid either way
anatomy.backdrop: the scrim, in that one cell. Painted under mode=overlay with modal only
anatomy.panel: the surface, in the same cell, aligned to the side. Two boxes and not three: dialog needs a viewport between the layer and the panel because its root is a query container, which makes a scrim inside a scrolling root part of what scrolls. A drawer's root declares no container and never scrolls, because the panel is bounded to the layer by construction
anatomy.resizer: --slotted-target-min thick, spanning the panel on the edge the reader reaches from. It is a row of the panel's grid on a block side and an overlay on the inner edge on an inline side, and the asymmetry has one cause: every rule in the panel runs across the inline axis, so a resizer row crosses none of them and a resizer column would cut all of them. The first capture showed exactly that — a rule under the header stopping twenty-four pixels short of the panel's own edge, which reads as an unfinished line rather than as a track. On an inline side the rows keep clear of it with an inset of max(the panel padding, the separator thickness)

scroll.body: the body scrolls; the header, the footer and the resizer stay
scroll.reason: There is no scroll axis, and dialog has one because a centred panel can be taller than the layer and the reader has to choose which box moves. A drawer's panel is exactly the layer's block extent on a side and its own extent on a top or bottom, so it never exceeds the layer and there is no second thing that could scroll. Ant, Fluent and MUI all scroll the body and none of them ships an axis for it

mount.active: the layer exists only while it is open, and @slotted/core/presence holds it through its own exit
mount.lazy: the layer is built on the first open and kept afterwards
mount.eager: the layer exists from the start and is inert while closed
mount.reason: The same reading dialog took: a layer transitions a translate that presence already keeps mounted, and a layer left in the document holds its controls in the page tab sequence. Under mode=inline the panel is always in the document, so the axis decides only whether its content is built

mode.overlay: portalled, fixed to the viewport, with a scrim and the whole dismissal policy
mode.inline: in the consumer's own layout, with no portal, no scrim, no z-index and no dismissal policy. The root's own size is what opens and closes
mode.reason: docs/component-features.md section 8 asks for both — modal ou persistente conforme viewport — so only the packaging is open. An axis rather than two components, because the switch is the point: two components mean the consumer swaps one element for another at a breakpoint, and both frameworks destroy the subtree when they do, taking the panel's scroll position, focus and every uncontrolled input with it
mode.responsive: The breakpoint is the consumer's. A family owning a viewport media query is what references/rubric.md dimension 3 refuses, and a container query cannot answer it because an overlay drawer has no place in the layout to measure. Fluent, MUI and Angular Material all document the consumer binding it

extent.unit: a fraction of the layer along the panel's own axis, in [0, 1], rather than a CSS length
extent.unset: the size step decides, through --_extent: var(--slotted-drawer-extent, var(--_step))
extent.property: --slotted-drawer-extent, written by the binding as an inline custom property once the reader has moved it. It is a theme-owned decision as well — an application setting one measure for every drawer writes it on [data-ui='drawer'] — which is why it is in drawer.tokens.json and not in packages/styles/src/runtime-properties.mjs
extent.step: 0.05 of the layer per arrow press, when there are no snap points
extent.snapPoints: an array of fractions, empty by default. With them an arrow moves to the adjacent stop, Home and End go to the first and last, a drag releases onto the nearest, and minExtent and maxExtent default to the first and the last
extent.dismissThreshold: a drag released below minExtent asks to close, carrying pointer; a close the consumer cancels leaves the panel at minExtent. That is what MUI's SwipeableDrawer and Vaul's dismiss gesture both do, expressed as a consequence of the resize rather than as a second mechanism
extent.overlapCost: On side=start the separator sits at the panel's inline-end edge, which is where a left-to-right document also puts the body's scrollbar. The wheel still scrolls and the scrollbar's inner half is still reachable, and every desktop application with a resizable sidebar has the same overlap
extent.capability: Rendering the resizer part is the capability. There is no resizable prop, so a resizable prop with no resizer part, and a resizer part a prop has switched off, are both states this family cannot be in
extent.reason: A fraction and not a length: the Window Splitter pattern's three aria values are then the fraction times a hundred, the limits and the snap points are the same kind of number so one clamp covers all three, and a keyboard step is a proportion rather than a pixel literal the family would have to tokenise

open.result: the value of the close part that was pressed

dialogElement.reason: The same decision dialog took, for the same reason: an element promoted to the top layer paints above every element in the document regardless of z-index, and every other overlay in this library is portalled and stacked with --slotted-z-index-overlay plus --slotted-layer-depth. A select opened inside a drawer would paint behind the drawer it belongs to
dialogElement.alsoCosts: An inline drawer could not be a dialog element at all, so the family would need two mechanisms rather than one, which is the opposite of what the mode axis exists for
dialogElement.cost: The family depends on JavaScript for containment, inertness and Escape under mode=overlay

scrollAxis.reason: See scroll above: a drawer's panel never exceeds the layer, so there is no second thing that could scroll

pushMode.reason: Angular Material's push and MUI's persistent shift the page content aside. mode=inline puts the drawer in the consumer's own grid or flex row, and the sibling reflows because the layout says so rather than because a family wrote a margin on an element it does not own

parentPush.reason: Ant's push slides a parent drawer aside when a child opens. The depth comes from dismissable-layer's single stack and the layers overlap; animating the parent would mean this family owning the geometry of a layer it no longer controls

panelDrag.reason: Vaul supports dragging the panel itself and spends most of its complexity there: telling a drag from a scroll, telling it from a text selection, and repositionInputs for the keyboard that opens under it. The resizer is the drag target, it is twenty-four pixels of real estate, and it is the same control the keyboard uses
panelDrag.cost: A reader cannot flick a bottom sheet away from its middle, and the resizer has to be rendered for the gesture to exist at all

drawerService.reason: The same decision dialog took. With @if and signals, opening a drawer from code is three lines in the consumer's own template, afterClosed() is the closed output carrying the same result, and the data injection is the component's own inputs, checked by the compiler rather than cast from a token

scrollStrategy.reason: A drawer is anchored to an edge of the layer rather than to an element, so reposition describes nothing; closing on scroll is a tooltip and popover policy; noop is modal=false, which is already an axis; and block is what the scroll lock does

emptyState.reason: An empty list inside a drawer is result-state, which owns the seven statuses and the marks that distinguish them without colour. A second empty state here would be a second answer to one question

positioner.reason: A drawer is anchored to an edge of the layer, not to an element, so there is nothing to position against and no collision to resolve

liveAnnouncer.reason: Under mode=overlay the dialog role announces the layer itself. Under mode=inline the trigger's aria-expanded is what a reader hears, which is what a disclosure already means

ariaValueText.reason: A reader hears 40 rather than 40 per cent. The string would have to be built from a locale this family does not take, and a hard-coded per-cent sign is wrong in the locales that place it differently. The Window Splitter pattern's 0 to 100 range is what makes the bare number legible
